title: Brazil's GSI plans to take a general cybersecurity law to the Creden, Exame reports
date_note: Exame gives only its own publication day, 25 November; the page gives no earlier day.
summary: Exame reports that Brazil's GSI wants to take the General Cybersecurity Law to the Creden at an extraordinary meeting planned for 2 December. GSI minister Marcos Antonio Amaro dos Santos announced the intention during Brasil Ciberseguro 2026. Exame says the TCU told the Casa Civil in November that without a law the policy may not reach the whole country, and that the meeting does not guarantee a vote in 2026.
plain: Exame reports that Brazil's security office wants to push a national cybersecurity law forward, but the meeting does not guarantee a vote this year.
exec: Exame reports Brazil may move toward a national cybersecurity law; the TCU says the current policy may not reach the whole country without one.
geo_basis: Federal government (GSI), Brasília; no other place stated

validation.note: Only Exame read; it relays the GSI minister and a TCU communication.

review.note: compared title, 25 Nov date, 2 Dec Creden meeting, minister, TCU statement, no-vote-guarantee against Exame
